{How did World Champion, Garry Kasparov, play a promising pawn sacrifice?} 6.
h4 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try to find a way to defend g5.] [%hint
Defend your bishop and prepare to open the h-file if Black captures.]} (6. Bxe7
$5 {This is a good move, but Kasparov chose to offer a strong gambit. What did
he play?}) (6. Be3 $5 {This is a good move, but Kasparov chose to offer a
strong gambit. What did he play?}) (6. f4 $2 Bxg5 {Black is slightly better.
Try again and look for another pawn move to defend the bishop.}) 6... Bxg5 {
This enters the dangerous Alekhine - Chatard Attack. What's next?} 7. hxg5 {
[%wrong Black is winning. Try again.] [%hint Recapture the piece.]} Qxg5 {
Great job! How did Kasparov justify his pawn sacrifice and attack Black's
h-pawn?} 8. Qd3 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try to find a way to develop
with a threat.] [%hint Develop a piece to target h7.]} (8. Nh3 $5 {This is a
good move, but Kasparov chose to attack h7. What did he play?}) (8. Nf3 $5 {
This is playable, but Kasparov preferred to attack h7. How did he do it?}) (8.
Nb5 $5 {This is playable, but Kasparov preferred to attack h7. How did he do
it?}) (8. Bd3 $2 Qxg2 {Black is doing well. Try again and look for a better
way to target the h7-pawn.}) 8... Nc6 {Good work! Black counter-attacked d4.
How did Kasparov continue?} 9. Nf3 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find
a way to develop with another threat.] [%hint Develop a piece to defend d4 and
attack g5.]} (9. Nh3 $5 {This is playable, but there's a better move. Try to
find a stronger square for the knight.}) (9. Nb5 $2 Qd8 {Black has a safe
position. Try again and look for a stronger threat.}) (9. Rxh7 $2 Rxh7 {
After Qxh7 and Nxd4 Black is better. Try again and look for a strong threat.})
(9. Nge2 $2 Nb4 {Black is doing well. Try to find a stronger square for the
knight.}) 9... Qg6 {Great job! Black offered a queen trade. Should you accept?}
10. Qxg6 {[%wrong There's a stronger option. Try to find a good capture.] 
[%hint Trade pieces to make Black recapture away from the center.]} (10. Qd2 $5
{This is a good move, but there's an even better one. Try to find a good
capture.}) 10... fxg6 {Nice move! How can you threaten to win back your
sacrificed pawn with interest?} 11. Nb5 {[%wrong There's a stronger option.
Try to find a powerful knight move.] [%hint Threaten a fork on c7.] Great
work! White has a powerful attack and went on to win a crushing game in
Kasparov - Kortchnoi, 2001.} (11. Bd3 $2 Nf8 {White is OK, but there's a
better move. Try to make a strong threat.}) (11. O-O-O $2 Nb6 {Both sides are
OK. See if you can make a strong threat.}) 1-0

{In the opening game of the 1960 World Championship, how did Mikhail Tal
develop with a threat against an undefended pawn?} 7. Qg4 {[%wrong There's a
better developing move that makes a threat. Try to find it.] [%hint Develop
your queen to attack g7.]} (7. Nf3 $5 {This is OK, but Tal played an
aggressive move to attack the g7-pawn. What was his choice?}) (7. Bd2 $5 {
This is OK, but Tal played an aggressive move to attack the g7-pawn. What was
his choice?}) (7. Bd3 $5 {This is OK, but Tal played an aggressive move to
attack the g7-pawn. What was his choice?}) (7. a4 $5 {This is a good move, but
Tal preferred to develop with a threat. How did he do it?}) (7. Rb1 $5 {
This is a good move, but Tal preferred to develop with a threat. How did he do
it?}) (7. h4 $5 {This is a good move, but Tal preferred to develop with a
threat. How did he do it?}) 7... f5 {Good start! How should you retreat the
queen, but keep an eye on g7?} 8. Qg3 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to
find a good queen retreat to maintain a threat against g7.] [%hint Retreat the
queen along the g-file.]} (8. Qh5+ $5 {This is OK, but Tal played a queen
retreat to keep pressure on g7. What was his choice?}) (8. exf6 $2 Nxf6 {
White's queen must retreat and Black has an active position. Try to find a
good queen move to keep pressure on g7.}) (8. Qg5 $2 cxd4 {The threat of Qxc3+
gives Black a good game. Try to find a stronger queen move.}) 8... Ne7 {
Good move! Black has sacrificed a pawn. Should you capture it?} 9. Qxg7 {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a good capture.] 
[%hint Capture an undefended pawn.]} (9. Bb5+ $5 {This is OK, but why not
capture a free pawn?}) (9. Bd2 $5 {This is OK, but why not capture a free pawn?
}) (9. dxc5 $2 O-O {Black is doing well and has the much better structure. Try
again and look for a good capture.}) 9... Rg8 {Good choice! Botvinnik aimed
for compensation by attacking on the g-file, but Tal found a good queen move.
Where did it go?} 10. Qxh7 {[%wrong There's a better move to save your queen.
Try to find it.] [%hint Save your queen and capture an undefended pawn.]} (10.
Qh6 $2 cxd4 {This is possible, but why not capture a pawn while you save your
queen?}) (10. Qf6 $2 cxd4 {Black has good counterplay. Try to find a stronger
queen move.}) 10... cxd4 {Way to grab material! What surprising move did Tal
play to avoid a check on c3?} 11. Kd1 {[%wrong There's a stronger move. Try to
find it and check the hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Hide your king on a light
square so Qxc3 won't be check.] Amazing move! Tal's idea is strong although,
nowadays most players choose the safer option, Ne2. We will revisit this great
game between Tal and Botvinnik in the next challenge.} (11. Ne2 $5 {This is
sensible, but Al preferred a cunning king move so that Qxc3 by Black wouldn't
be a check. What was his idea?}) (11. Qh5+ $5 {This is sensible, but Al
preferred a cunning king move so that Qxc3 by Black wouldn't be a check. What
was his idea?}) (11. cxd4 $2 Qc3+ {Black wins material. Try to find a Tal's
cunning king move.}) (11. Bd2 $2 Qxe5+ {Black is doing well. Try to find Tal's
cunning king move.}) (11. Kd2 $2 Qxc3+ {Black will win material. Try to find a
safer king move.}) (11. Ke2 $2 Qc4+ {Black will win material. Try to find a
safer king move.}) 1-0
